name: BNC panel jack, 50 ohm, solder cup and ground tag (Amphenol RF 31-221-RFX)
blurb: The bayonet socket that probe and antenna cables twist onto. It goes through a hole in the case wall and is held by a nut; the signal wire is soldered to the pin at the back and ground to a tag under the nut.

pins.name: SIG
pins.note: The centre contact: the small tube (solder cup) sticking out of the middle of the back. Push the stripped wire into the cup and solder.

pins.name: GND
pins.note: The metal shell. Solder to the hole in the loose ring tag that sits on the thread under the nut, inside the case; it can point any way, it is drawn pointing up. The shell also touches a metal panel directly, so in a metal case the case becomes ground.

search: BNC bulkhead jack solder cup front mount 50 ohm
BNC panel mount female socket solder nut

verify: From the Amphenol RF customer drawing of 31-221-RFX: panel hole 9.7 mm with one flat at 8.85 mm (a plain 9.7 mm round hole also works, the flat only stops it turning); thread 3/8 inch-32 UNEF; panel no thicker than 3.3 mm, so a 3 mm printed wall is the limit and the nut has little thread left: thin the wall around the hole if it does not catch. Flange 12.7 mm, overall length 26.9 mm (reference), nut 11 mm (7/16 inch) across flats and 2.4 mm thick, lock washer 12.7 x 0.5 mm, ground tag hole 1.6 mm at 12.7 mm from the axis, solder cup 2.1 mm outside and 1.5 mm inside. It mounts from outside: the bayonet body and the flange stay outside the wall. How far the flange is from the front is not dimensioned on the sheet; scaled off the drawing it is about 10.6 mm, which leaves about 15 mm inside the case with a thin wall. The tag is drawn 15 mm from the front and 3.2 mm wide for recognition; its real place depends on the wall thickness. Drawn as a block lying on its side with the mating end at y = 0; the real part is round. 50 ohm, 1000 V RMS withstand. A mating BNC plug is about 15 mm across and needs room to be twisted. Cheap unbranded BNC panel jacks use the same hole but check their length.
